Clothes & getting dressed

heel noun

of a shoe

modern

Traupman 327

fulmentum, fulmentī n.

noun, second declension

heel of a shoe

Classically a prop or support.

Examples

  • fulmenta calceōrum ad canthum rotae posteriōris admovet et terendō cursum tardat

    he puts the heels of his shoes to the back tyre and slows down by rubbingFābula VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

See also shoe.

SourcesLewis & Short: fulmentum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 327, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater: Fābulae Latīnae ad vītam cotīdiānam I–VII, as revised on 29 October 2026. Examples marked “Fābula” quote those texts word for word.
